/-!
# Erdős Problem 982

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/982](https://www.erdosproblems.com/982)
-/

@[expose] public section

open EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos982

/--
If $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then some vertex has at least
$\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$ different distances to other vertices.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_982 (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (p : Fin n → ℝ²) (hp : Function.Injective p)
    (hp' : EuclideanGeometry.IsConvexPolygon p) :
    ∃ (i : Fin n), { d : ℝ | ∃ j : Fin n, j ≠ i ∧ d = dist (p i) (p j) }.ncard ≥ n / 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos982

reformulations.difference: The source describes an unordered vertex set, whereas Lean uses an injective tuple whose indexing follows a convex polygon's boundary in either orientation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every convex polygon's vertex set admits a cyclic boundary enumeration. The consistent nonzero orientation condition in IsConvexPolygon characterizes such an enumeration. Relabelling preserves each vertex's set of distances and hence the existential cardinality bound. In scratch.lean, ordered_iff_reorderable proves that the stated universal claim is equivalent to the version allowing arbitrary labellings that admit a convex boundary-order relabelling; conclusion_reindex proves the required invariance.

sources_consulted: Nivasch, Pach, Pinchasi, and Zerbib, The number of distinct distances from a vertex of a convex polygon, arXiv:1207.1266v2, abstract, introduction, and concluding remarks; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1207.1266v2
review.notes: No mathematical defects found. Natural-number division gives the required floor. The distance set is always finite, so Set.ncard's infinite-set default is unreachable; injectivity excludes distance zero. Scratch checks compiled successfully and include the n=3 boundary case, a nondegenerate triangle satisfying the hypotheses, the square distance set {1, sqrt 2} with cardinality 2, and equivalence after adding the trivial n=2 case mentioned in the primary paper. The archived source and current Erdős database both record the problem as unresolved ('falsifiable'), consistent with research open. Live erdosproblems.com requests were blocked by Cloudflare, so the source text and remarks were read through the archive and corroborated by the primary paper. The reviewed file was not modified.
